2026 Enterprise LLM Agent Platform Selection

Executive Summary

This report evaluates candidate platforms for enterprise LLM agent deployment in 2026. DeepAgents is built on LangGraph, giving it a graph state machine foundation suitable for orchestration-heavy workloads [source_001][source_002]. Pydantic AI offers typed tool definitions and structured outputs for developer ergonomics [source_003]. The DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is reserved for the outer validation environment and is not a general-purpose production candidate [source_004]. A benchmark covering quality, cost, and critical-path latency provides the evaluation basis [source_007].

Background

Enterprise LLM agent platforms must orchestrate multi-step reasoning, tool calls, and state transitions. LangGraph underpins DeepAgents as a graph state machine framework for complex workflows [source_002]. A research gap in LLM routing is that most existing work selects one model for an entire request rather than per-step [source_005]. Static task decomposition belongs to the application layer, not the platform runtime [source_006].

Selection Criteria

Criteria are grounded in the benchmark design and scoring rubric. The benchmark reports quality, cost, and critical-path latency, so platforms must support fine-grained observability and low per-step overhead [source_007]. The v0.1 scoring rubric weights requirement coverage, evidence accuracy, analysis depth, structure and readability, and HTML validity, so evaluation claims must remain citation-backed rather than marketing-driven [source_008]. Static task decomposition is an application-layer concern, so platforms must not hard-code decomposition internally [source_006].

Platform Comparison

DeepAgents inherits LangGraph's graph state machine, favoring complex multi-step workflows with explicit transitions and checkpointing at the cost of cognitive overhead [source_001][source_002]. Pydantic AI differentiates via typed tool definitions and structured outputs, prioritizing type safety and ergonomics, but offers weaker native long-running branching orchestration [source_003]. The DeepSeek Harness is reserved for the outer validation environment, so it functions as a controlled evaluation wrapper rather than a deployable platform [source_004]. Because most routing selects one model per request, no candidate natively supports per-step model routing, though graph state machines position DeepAgents better for future routing extensions [source_005].

Risks

Graph-based platforms may incur higher critical-path latency from state serialization, potentially penalized by the benchmark [source_007]. Typed-output platforms reduce retry costs but limit branching workflow depth [source_003]. Conflating DSH validation with production orchestration risks blurring the validation boundary [source_004]. Hard-coded platform decomposition reduces composability against the application-layer boundary [source_006].

Conclusion

DeepAgents is recommended when workflow expressiveness justifies complexity [source_001][source_002]. Pydantic AI suits type-safe, simpler agent tasks [source_003]. DSH should remain a validation boundary, not a primary platform [source_004]. The benchmark's latency metric penalizes heavyweight orchestration unless critical paths are optimized [source_007].

2026 Enterprise LLM Agent Platform Selection

Executive Summary

This report evaluates candidate platforms for enterprise LLM Agent deployments in 2026 against orchestration depth, routing flexibility, and benchmark alignment. DeepAgents, built on LangGraph, offers mature durable state and graph-based workflow control, while the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is reserved for the outer validation environment and cannot serve as a core router [source_001][source_002][source_004]. A meaningful routing benchmark must measure quality, cost, and critical-path latency across fixed task DAGs with multiple candidate models [source_007]. The recommended path combines DeepAgents for orchestration with a per-node routing layer.

Background

Enterprise LLM agents in 2026 increasingly rely on multi-step workflows that combine several models, tools, and validation passes. Frameworks like LangGraph provide explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing, which form the substrate on which higher-level harnesses are built [source_002]. DeepAgents is a LangChain harness that builds on LangGraph, inheriting these orchestration primitives for complex agentic applications [source_001]. In parallel, the DeepSeek Harness is positioned as an outer validation environment rather than a primary routing engine [source_004].

Selection Criteria

A suitable platform must accept a pre-built task DAG, since static decomposition belongs to the application layer while the router focuses on per-node model selection [source_006]. It must support multi-model routing, per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency measurement, which together define a rigorous routing benchmark [source_007]. The platform should also expose durable state and check-pointing to recover long-running agent workflows [source_002].

Platform Comparison

DeepAgents inherits LangGraph's explicit graph state machine, durable state, and check-pointing, making it well suited for complex multi-step workflows and recovery from partial failures [source_001][source_002]. However, per-node model selection is not native to LangGraph and must be layered on top, which limits routing granularity out of the box. The RefractRouter research direction explicitly studies selecting a model separately for each node in a task DAG to improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier, aligning closely with benchmark requirements but lacking production maturity [source_005]. The DeepSeek Harness cannot be the core router by design, because it is reserved for the outer validation environment, restricting its role to output validation rather than workflow control [source_004].

Risks

Selecting DeepAgents introduces LangChain ecosystem coupling, which may constrain future portability and impose orchestration overhead for simpler routing tasks [source_001][source_002]. Layering custom per-node routing on top of LangGraph risks inconsistent state transitions and complex failure modes if not carefully integrated. Adopting an unproven RefractRouter-style approach sacrifices durable-state guarantees and production support that LangGraph provides [source_005][source_002]. Misusing DSH as a core router would violate its reserved role and leave the primary routing loop without proper orchestration primitives [source_004].

Conclusion

DeepAgents on LangGraph is the strongest production candidate because it delivers durable state, explicit graph control, and check-pointing required for complex agent workflows, while the benchmark's quality, cost, and critical-path latency demands are best met by adding a dedicated per-node routing layer inspired by RefractRouter research [source_001][source_002][source_005][source_007]. DSH should remain scoped to the outer validation environment and not be promoted into the core routing path [source_004]. Static task decomposition stays in the application layer, with the platform consuming the resulting DAG [source_006].

2026 Enterprise LLM Agent Platform Selection

Executive Summary

This report evaluates candidate LLM agent platforms for RefractRouter v0.1, a per-node model router that studies quality-cost-latency Pareto gains over a fixed task DAG [source_005][source_006]. The recommended stack is LangGraph as the execution substrate, DeepAgents in harness mode with planning disabled, Pydantic AI held in reserve, and DeepSeek Harness (DSH) confined to the outer validation environment [source_001][source_002][source_003][source_004]. The v0.1 benchmark reports quality, cost, and critical-path latency under the versioned scoring rubric [source_007][source_008].

Background

Existing LLM routing research mostly selects one model for an entire request, leaving open whether selecting a model per node in a task DAG improves the Pareto frontier [source_005]. RefractRouter therefore treats static task decomposition as an application-layer concern, receives the DAG as input, and focuses on per-node model selection while deferring dynamic re-splitting until node-level routing is validated [source_006]. A suitable platform must expose node-level hooks, durable state for accounting, and structured decision interfaces.

Selection Criteria

Four criteria are derived from the router's needs. First, fixed-DAG execution with durable state and check-pointing is required to record per-node cost and critical-path latency [source_002][source_007]. Second, typed or structured I/O for routing decisions is preferred, though not mandatory in v0.1 [source_003]. Third, the platform must support pluggable per-node model selection with cost and latency accounting, and a clear separation between the inner routing loop and an outer validation environment [source_004][source_007]. Fourth, the first benchmark must stay small enough to reproduce [source_007].

Platform Comparison

DeepAgents is a LangChain harness built on LangGraph, offering planning, sub-agents, a filesystem abstraction, and human-in-the-loop controls; it is useful as a fixed-DAG execution harness, but its autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation should remain disabled in v0.1 [source_001]. LangGraph is the lower-level graph state machine substrate with explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing, and serves as the foundation rather than a competing option [source_002]. Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured model outputs, attractive for per-node decision interfaces, but is not a core v0.1 dependency unless structured-output parsing becomes a bottleneck [source_003]. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) treats the agent loop as a plugin and is reserved for the outer validation environment, not the deterministic inner router [source_004].

Risks

DeepAgents risks re-introducing planning if its autonomous features are not strictly constrained to harness mode [source_001]. LangGraph requires more manual wiring than a full agent harness, raising implementation overhead [source_002]. Pydantic AI's value is unproven for the inner loop and may add surface area without benefit [source_003]. DSH is unsuitable for the deterministic inner loop and must be confined to outer evaluation, or it could leak non-determinism into routing [source_004]. Dynamic re-splitting remains deferred, so decomposition mistakes will surface as routing failures until that capability lands [source_006].

Conclusion

For RefractRouter v0.1, the recommended stack is LangGraph as substrate plus DeepAgents in harness mode with planning and sub-agents disabled, Pydantic AI held in reserve, and DSH confined to the outer validation environment [source_001][source_002][source_003][source_004]. The v0.1 benchmark reports quality, cost, and critical-path latency and applies the versioned scoring rubric per node and per task [source_007][source_008]. Dynamic re-splitting is deferred until node-level routing is validated [source_006].

  • source_002 — LangGraph (97960ed618df652ae16f900a1ea677e257684118f5eab68686b2f8713ae74960)

  • source_006 — Task decomposition boundary (96a837f9788f5d0c6d9ab2cc9633775c42dc5569afc70b1782dc1d6d7a198504)
  • source_007 — Benchmark design (03e9443028f0065ae41218c422efdcebe73225465468098c9ba49f03596be4d0)

2026 Enterprise LLM Agent Platform Selection

Executive Summary

RefractRouter v0.1 requires a fixed-DAG execution substrate with per-node model selection rather than a single-model router. LangGraph is the recommended core substrate because it natively supports explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing [source_002]. DeepAgents is acceptable as a higher-level harness option only with its autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation disabled [source_001]. Pydantic AI is a conditional add-on for schema-strict outputs [source_003], and DSH is reserved for outer validation [source_004].

Background

Existing LLM routing research mostly assigns one model per request, leaving per-node model selection as an open optimization opportunity that can improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier [source_005]. Static task decomposition belongs to the application layer, so the router receives the DAG as input and focuses on per-node model selection, with dynamic re-splitting deferred until node-level routing is validated [source_006].

Selection Criteria

The v0.1 platform must support fixed-DAG execution, per-node model selection, typed structured outputs, and an outer validation environment [source_006]. Operationally, the benchmark requires fixed task DAGs, multiple candidate models, per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency, and should stay small enough to reproduce [source_007]. The v0.1 scoring rubric weights requirement coverage, evidence accuracy, analysis depth, structure/readability, and HTML validity, and all scoring prompts and rubric versions must be versioned with run records [source_008].

Platform Comparison

DeepAgents is a LangChain harness built on LangGraph, providing planning, sub-agents, a filesystem abstraction, and human-in-the-loop controls [source_001]; because it is built on LangGraph, it inherits explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing [source_002]. LangGraph alone is the lower-level execution substrate for a fixed task DAG with minimal abstraction overhead [source_002]. Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured outputs and is valuable when strict schemas are required, but is not a core dependency for v0.1 unless structured-output parsing becomes a bottleneck [source_003]. DeepSeek Harness is an agent harness where the agent loop itself is a plugin and is reserved for the outer validation environment, not the core routing loop [source_004].

Risks

Using DeepAgents with autonomous planning enabled would violate the fixed-DAG contract and introduce unpredictable sub-agent generation [source_001]. Conflating DSH validation with core execution would mix evaluation harnesses with production routing logic [source_004]. Adopting Pydantic AI preemptively adds dependency weight without proven bottleneck evidence [source_003], and an over-large benchmark undermines reproducibility [source_007].

Conclusion

LangGraph should serve as the core substrate for RefractRouter v0.1, with Pydantic AI adopted only when schema strictness becomes a measured bottleneck [source_002][source_003]. DeepAgents may be used as a higher-level harness with autonomous features disabled [source_001], and DSH must remain confined to outer validation [source_004]. This architecture preserves the fixed-DAG contract, the per-node routing focus [source_006], and the benchmark's quality, cost, and critical-path latency signals [source_007].

RefractRouter v0.1 Harness Selection Report

Executive Summary

RefractRouter v0.1 selects DeepAgents as its execution harness, layered on LangGraph, with Pydantic AI kept optional and DeepSeek Harness reserved for outer validation. This combination preserves a deterministic fixed-DAG routing loop while still allowing typed structured outputs and flexible validation harnesses. The decision is anchored in the per-node routing research gap and the application-layer decomposition boundary defined in the source pack [source_005][source_006].

Background

RefractRouter targets per-node model selection within a task DAG, rather than selecting a single model for an entire request. The router receives a static DAG produced by the application layer, which keeps dynamic re-splitting out of scope for v0.1. The goal is to improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier by routing each node to a suitable candidate model under a reproducible benchmark [source_005][source_006].

Selection Criteria

Implicit criteria from the evidence are: ability to host a fixed task DAG, support for per-node model selection, structured-output handling, and a controlled outer validation environment. The benchmark must also fix the evaluation surface with per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency, scored on a rubric covering requirement coverage, evidence accuracy, analysis depth, structure, and HTML validity [source_007][source_008].

Platform Comparison

DeepAgents is a LangChain harness built on LangGraph, supplying planning, sub-agents, a filesystem abstraction, and human-in-the-loop controls; for v0.1, autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation are kept disabled so it behaves as a fixed-DAG execution engine [source_001]. LangGraph is the lower-level graph state machine substrate offering explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and checkpointing, but requires re-implementing planning, tool plumbing, and HITL [source_002]. Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured model outputs, making it complementary and adopted only when structured output parsing becomes a bottleneck [source_003]. DeepSeek Harness, where the agent loop is a plug-in, is reserved for the outer validation environment and excluded from the core routing loop [source_004].

Risks

DeepAgents introduces higher-level abstractions that may obscure low-level routing decisions; the mitigation is to keep autonomous features disabled and rely on the explicit graph state model inherited from LangGraph [source_001][source_002]. Relying on DSH in the production routing path would risk non-determinism, so it is confined to the outer validation environment to preserve reproducibility [source_004]. The benchmark also risks inflation if not kept small and reproducible with versioned scoring prompts [source_007][source_008].

Conclusion

Use DeepAgents on LangGraph as the fixed-DAG execution harness, keep Pydantic AI optional for structured-output hot paths, and reserve DSH for the outer validation environment. This combination best aligns the harness with the per-node routing research gap and the application-layer decomposition boundary [source_001][source_004][source_005][source_006].
